analysis.session_summary: Risk-off dominated the full trading day: JPY strengthened 0.658% and CHF 0.469% while AUD fell 0.592% and NZD 0.357%, with VIX up 9.2% and DXY only -0.068%. Event reactions were mostly muted—US UoM basket 0.000%, Trump 0.013%, Lagarde -0.022%—and most zigzag legs had no clear catalyst. GBP retail sales was the one normal reaction, giving GBP a 0.066% boost that faded. The tape shows safe-haven demand and high-beta selling without a single dominant fundamental trigger.

themes.theme: Muted event reactions left price action flow-driven
themes.evidence: Revised UoM basket 0.000%, Trump 0.013%, Lagarde -0.022%; most legs had no clear catalyst.

currency_drivers.USD: Only muted UoM and Trump events; sold to -0.21% then recovered 63%, closing flat.
currency_drivers.EUR: Lagarde was muted; EUR sold to -0.22% and recovered 64% without a clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own releases; safe-haven bid took it to +0.658%, closed at its best.
currency_drivers.GBP: Retail sales beat gave a normal +0.066% boost that faded; closed -0.035%.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own releases; fell 0.592% to bottom of range with no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CAD: No own releases; slipped 0.07% with no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own releases; gained 0.469% on safe-haven demand and held range.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; fell 0.357% on risk-off, held range.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through seven alternating legs inside its 42.6-pip range, closing at 1.09729 (-5.4 pips); only the UoM leg (15:45-16:30) had a medium-confidence USD catalyst, and the final down leg had no clear cause.

polarity_reads.read: Muted move with basket 0.000% shows USD not positioned for a data surprise; selling into the event was quickly faded. AUD/USD was the most sensitive mover at -0.063% (-4.2 pips), but the aggregate was noise.

Basket was muted (0.013%), but high-beta and commodity FX showed significant sensitivity—NZD/CHF -0.1% sigma -3.13, USD/ZAR +0.137%, AUD/USD -0.09%. This implies the market treats Trump headlines as a risk-off/EM-negative impulse, not a clean USD event.
Normal polarity with GBP +0.066% on a beat shows no crowded short GBP; the move was modest and faded, suggesting GBP upside is not chasing data.
Muted -0.022% and no sustained EUR impulse; EUR was not positioned for hawkish or dovish surprise, leaving EUR cross-driven.

scenarios.name: Risk-off persist (safe-haven extension)
scenarios.thesis: Risk-off tone continues with VIX elevated and no catalyst to reverse; JPY and CHF stay bid while high-beta AUD/NZD under pressure.
scenarios.invalidation: A strong US services PMI or positive geopolitical news reverses the safe-haven bid.

pair_paths.rationale: Safe-haven JPY bid persists; USD/JPY already fell 106.9 pips, next leg can test lower.
EUR catalyst-free selling; 42.6-pip range allows 30 pips downside.
AUD weakest with no catalyst; 54.7-pip range gives room to extend lower.

scenarios.name: Risk stabilizes / mean reversion
scenarios.thesis: Risk-off eases and high-beta currencies bounce off lows as PMIs show stable growth, taking profit on JPY/CHF longs.
triggers: French/German PMIs not as weak as feared
scenarios.invalidation: A fresh geopolitical shock or sharply weak PMIs reassert safe-haven demand.

pair_paths.rationale: AUD bounces from 0.66316 low inside its 54.7-pip range.
Profit-taking on JPY longs unwinds some of the 106.9-pip drop.
EUR/USD stays within its 42.6-pip range with no fresh catalyst.

scenarios.name: USD-led data beat
scenarios.thesis: Strong US flash PMIs lift USD and unwind safe-haven trades; EUR/GBP lag.
scenarios.invalidation: PMIs miss or geopolitical headlines worsen.

pair_paths.rationale: USD strength unwinds safe-haven JPY bid, retracing part of the 129.0-pip range.
EUR softness meets USD bid; 42.6-pip range supports a 40-pip push lower.
GBP fades after retail sales boost; 50.5-pip range allows 35 pips downside.

risks.why_it_matters: PMIs are the first hard data of the session and can break the no-catalyst drift.
VIX already up 9.2%; Trump headlines moved NZD/CHF -3.13 sigma.
USD selling was rejected and DXY -0.068% only, leaving two-way risk.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Next session's flash PMIs from France, Germany, UK, and US can change the picture: weak EZ PMIs would extend EUR selling, strong US services PMI could lift USD/JPY, and any PMI surprise may dominate given today's muted reactions.
